decision_conditions:
Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall begin not later than three years from the date of this decision.

Reason: In order to comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: Unnumbered Existing Plans, Unnumbered Existing Elevations, Unnumbered Site Location Plan, Unnumbered Existing and Proposed Site Plan, Unnumbered Proposed Block Plan, Unnumbered Proposed Ground Floor Plan, Unnumbered Proposed First Floor Plan, Unnumbered Proposed Roof Plan, Unnumbered Proposed Elevations, Unnumbered Proposed Section AA, Unnumbered Design and Access Statement, Unnumbered Heritage Statement, Unnumbered Fire Statement, Unnumbered Flood Risk Assessment. Received: 15/01/2026
Unnumbered Existing and Proposed Flood Defence Wall Plan, Unnumbered Proposed Flood Defence Section. Received: 20/02/2026.
Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.

Condition : 3 - The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted shall match those used in the existing building, unless otherwise shown on the approved plans.
Reason: In order to safeguard the appearance of the area.

Condition : 4 - The roof area of the extension hereby permitted shall not be used as a balcony, roof garden or similar amenity area.
Reason: In order to protect neighbours' privacy

Condition : 5 - Visual Survey and Remedial Works Plan 
Prior to the commencement of development, a visual survey of the flood defence structures (upper and lower wall), as detailed in drawing PA/54Church/1225/FloodXSec and associated remedial works plan shall be submitted to the LPA in consultation with the Environment Agency. This will include: 
� The visual survey will include the upper and lower flood defence wall and will consider any defects associated with masonry and reinforced concrete structures, in addition to any obvious local or global instability of the structures.  
� A remedial works plan is required to detail how the defects, if any, identified in the visual survey are to be rectified and how the flood defence will be proactively monitored and maintained for the lifetime of the development. 
Reason: To ensure that there is no increase in flood risk and to protect the users of the site for the lifetime of the development, in line with paragraph 181 of the NPPF and 
Policy GB5 (Blue Ribbon Network) of the Hounslow Local Plan.
